applicabilityBasis.summary: CFX currently markets tokenized deposits in beneficiary bank accounts, while its July 2025 issuer release expressly describes CFX-issued MOVEUSD as a 1:1 redeemable stablecoin. Public website terms and withdrawal API documentation do not establish that each MOVEUSD holder has a legally enforceable deposit claim against an insured depository institution. Governing holder/account agreements remain necessary to distinguish an excluded deposit from an apparent payment stablecoin.

genius.licensingRegulator: Mississippi Department of Banking and Consumer Finance (money transmitter); FinCEN MSB registration is issuer-reported
genius.notes: CFX Labs Inc. is corroborated by the Mississippi money-transmitter list and retained verbatim as the issuer entity. The FinCEN registration statement is issuer-reported. GENIUS-ready and designed-to-comply descriptions identify architecture, without formal issuer permission, a filed application or a specified permission pathway; issuer-announced-intent is not assigned. Published 1:1 redemption claims and withdrawal mechanics support policy presence, but do not establish unrestricted retail fiat redemption or legally excluded deposits. No token-level reserve report or monthly independent attestation was located in current public documentation. Ordinary money-transmitter and partner-bank status do not establish GENIUS approval. No matching public regulator enforcement action was found in the bounded domain search. Section 20 sets the Act's effective date to January 18, 2027 or 120 days after implementing final regulations, whichever is earlier; no earlier-triggering final rules were located in the reviewed materials. The distinct general DASP offer/sale gate in section 3(b)(1) starts July 18, 2028. No current GENIUS offer/sale prohibition is asserted.

negativeEvidenceReview.summary: No token-specific PPSI approval, state qualification, official GENIUS application or registered foreign exception was located for MOVEUSD / CFX Labs Inc. in the opened sources and bounded name searches. Published proposals and bank/money-transmitter licenses do not establish GENIUS permission. This review is limited to public materials and does not establish that an authorization or nonpublic application cannot exist.
